archetypes.name: state-machine
archetypes.rationale: The plan hinges on publish outcome state, sentinels, pause/resume reentry, and contradictory rc/stdout handling across multiple paths.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the proposed Step 5c, Step 0b clarify, design-publish, and pause-save state transitions against the scoped files. Look for plan defects where SESSION_ID, PUBLISH_OK, PLAN_WRITE_OK, exit codes, sentinels, rename, or reentry-marker behavior can drift from the intended matrix. Verify the plan targets the actual writer of each state artifact and does not leave a resume path that advances or skips incorrectly. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: contract-sync
archetypes.rationale: The change spans script envelopes, markdown contracts, SECURITY.md, and harness docs, creating high drift risk between behavior and documentation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the written plan against the repository's documented contracts for publish envelopes, argv failures, run-log summary behavior, and design workflow semantics. Hunt for mismatches between proposed script changes and the paired .md files, SECURITY.md, SKILL.md prose, and test documentation. Pay special attention to whether exit-1 malformed repo behavior is consistently carved out without corrupting existing PUBLISH_OK=false operational-failure contracts. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: callsite-boundaries
archetypes.rationale: Adding strict --repo validation and changing nonzero publish handling can break or expose direct and indirect caller boundaries.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every scoped callsite of design-log-publish.sh and related publish wrappers against the proposed validation and fail-closed behavior. Check whether all callers pre-resolve or validate repo values, handle exit 1 safely, and avoid trusting stdout success on nonzero exits. Look for missing plan steps around malformed OWNER/REPO inputs, newline or traversal cases, hub-default behavior, and security-relevant operator diagnostics. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
